caption: The drawing depicts a single intricately designed pitcher or jug centered against a plain, off-white background. The vessel is sketched in grayscale pencil and features a tall, angular body with two horizontal decorative bands encircling it; both bands are adorned with floral or leaf motifs. The jug has a wide, flared base and a gradually tapering neck that leads to a domed lid. On top of the lid is a sculpted head in profile, possibly representing a classical figure, with elaborate curly hair and a scroll-like handle extending from the head’s back. The handle of the pitcher also incorporates a sculpted human head at its top attachment point, with the rest of the handle arching gracefully and joining the jug’s middle section. The drawing is signed “HARRY MANN WADDELL” near the lower right corner. The entire composition is rendered with careful shading to suggest metallic texture and depth, and there are no additional objects or background elements present.
title: Pewter Syrup Jar
